findings.summary: Page 2 (multi-stage builds) opens with a Compose YAML fragment that uses Compose syntax, healthchecks and named volumes, none of which have been introduced yet.
findings.evidence: First block of page 2: `  db:` / `    image: postgres:16` / `    healthcheck:` / `      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"]` / `      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`, note "named volume declared at top level" — volumes are defined on page 3 and Compose on page 6.
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 2 and relocate it to the Compose example on page 7; start page 2 with the '3. Multi-Stage Example' heading.

findings.summary: The 'web + db' Compose example is split in half, with the `db` service definition printed five pages earlier on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 7 shows only `services:` / `web:` / `build: .` / `depends_on:` / `db:` / `condition: service_healthy` with the note "condition needs a healthcheck on db", while the matching `db:` / `image: postgres:16` / `healthcheck:` / `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` / `volumes: pgdata: {}` block is the first block of page 2.
findings.fix: Move the `db:` + top-level `volumes:` YAML block from page 2 to page 7, directly beneath the `web:` snippet, so the reader sees one complete compose file.

findings.summary: The registry worked example (section 3) is taught on page 8, before the registry definition and push/pull mechanics (sections 1 and 2) that appear on page 9.
findings.evidence: Page 8 ends with `3. Example: Publish to GHCR` and `docker login ghcr.io` / `docker tag myapp:1.0 ...` / `docker push ...`; page 9 then begins with `1. What a Registry Is` — "==Registry==: HTTP service that stores and serves image **layers** and **manifests**" and `2. Push and Pull Mechanics`.
findings.fix: Move sections 1 and 2 (registry definition, push/pull flow diagram) onto page 8 ahead of the GHCR example, and keep sections 3–6 on page 9 in numeric order.

findings.summary: The heading '4. Resource Limits' has no content under it — no memory, cpu, pids or log-size flags are ever shown, yet the page's takeaway tells the reader to always set them.
findings.evidence: `{"type":"heading","text":"4. Resource Limits"}` is followed only by a cards diagram whose limits card says "memory, cpus, pids, log size via cgroups"; the takeaway claims "Always set memory, cpus, pids and log limits" but `--memory 512m`, `--cpus 1`, `--pids-limit 100` and `--log-opt max-size=10m max-file=3` appear nowhere on the page.
findings.fix: Add a bullets or code block under '4. Resource Limits' showing `docker run --memory 512m --memory-swap 512m --cpus 1 --pids-limit 100 --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3`, plus the note that an unlimited container can OOM the host.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label rather than a hook, so the only line visible before Instagram's "more" cut-off has no pull.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER COMPLETE NOTES. Ever wondered what actually happens when you type docker run?"
findings.fix: Lead with the question and move the part label after it: "Ever wondered what actually happens when you type docker run? Part 2 of DOCKER COMPLETE NOTES takes you from namespaces and cgroups to Compose, registries and production hardening."

findings.summary: Page 1 carries three code blocks about registries, digests and volume backups — topics introduced five to eight pages later — inside the build-cache lesson.
findings.evidence: Page 1 contains `# self-hosted registry` / `docker run -d -p 5000:5000 registry:2` with note "HTTP registries must be in daemon.json", `docker image inspect myapp:1.0 --format '{{.RepoDigests}}'` / `docker pull myapp@sha256:3f1a...` with note "digest pull = immutable deploy", and `# backup a named volume to host` / `docker run --rm -v data:/from -v $(pwd):/to alpine tar czf ...`.
findings.fix: Move the two registry blocks to the registry pages (8–9) and the volume-backup block to page 4 beside the volume commands; keep only build-cache code on page 1.

findings.summary: Page 1 jumps from section 2 straight to '5. Common Mistakes', so the mistakes are read before sections 3 and 4 that they refer to.
findings.evidence: Page 1 headings run `1. Layers and the Cache`, `2. Cache Invalidation`, `5. Common Mistakes`; page 2 then has `3. Multi-Stage Example`, `4. Base Image Comparison`, `6. Key Takeaways`.
findings.fix: Re-flow the spill so sections 3 and 4 finish before section 5: keep 1–3 on page 1 and 4–6 on page 2.

findings.summary: BuildKit cache and secret mount syntax is shown as code on page 1 before BuildKit itself is explained on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 code: `RUN --mount=type=cache,\  target=/root/.npm npm ci` and `RUN --mount=type=secret,\  id=tok cat /run/secrets/tok`; the explanation "BuildKit (default) builds independent stages in **parallel**", "`RUN --mount=type=cache` keeps package caches between builds" only arrives in page 2's bullets.
findings.fix: Move the BuildKit code block to page 2 immediately after the BuildKit bullets, or move those bullets onto page 1 above the code.

findings.summary: The "Named volume" card's path text overflows the card's right border and the final character is clipped.
findings.evidence: The card body reads "Docker-managed under /var/lib/docker/volume ; portable, backed up with docker tools" — the path runs into the card border with the "s" of "/var/lib/docker/volumes" cut off.
findings.fix: Shorten the card text to "Docker-managed under /var/lib/docker/volumes; portable, backed up with docker tools" with a smaller mono size or allow the path to wrap inside the card instead of overflowing.

findings.summary: Page 4 opens with '5. Common Mistakes' for volumes, placed before sections 3 and 4 which teach the mount rules those mistakes depend on.
findings.evidence: Block order on page 4 is `5. Common Mistakes` → `3. Mount Rules in Practice` → `4. Named Volume vs Bind Mount`; the mistake "Bind mount + container root: files on host owned by **root**" precedes the section explaining how bind mounts shadow image files.
findings.fix: Reorder page 4 to 3 → 4 → volume commands → 5 → takeaways.

findings.summary: Page 4 ends with orphaned lead-ins for two later topics — networking cards and the Compose intro paragraph — while the volumes chapter is still on the page.
findings.evidence: After the volume takeaways, page 4 carries a cards diagram ("Net Namespace", "Bridge", "Embedded DNS", "Port Publish") and the paragraph "Compose turns a pile of `docker run` commands into ==one YAML file==...", but Compose does not begin until page 6.
findings.fix: Keep the networking cards as the opener of page 5 and move the Compose paragraph to page 6 directly above '1. What Compose Is'.

findings.summary: The `--add-host` command in the "EXAMPLE: WEB TALKS TO DB" box is cut off at the right page edge, losing the end of the flag value.
findings.evidence: Renders as "--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gatewa" — the trailing "y" of "host-gateway" is clipped where the line runs past the dashed box border into the page margin.
findings.fix: Shorten or wrap that bullet so the flag fits the column, e.g. break after "Linux needs" and place `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` on its own wrapped line inside the box width.

findings.summary: The networking Key Takeaways on page 5 summarize the host, none and overlay drivers, which are not taught until the driver comparison table on page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5's final checkbox bullet reads "host = speed, none = isolation, overlay = many hosts", while `4. Comparison: Network Drivers` with rows `host`, `none`, `overlay`, `macvlan` appears on page 6.
findings.fix: Move section 4 (driver comparison) ahead of page 5's mistakes and takeaways, or drop the driver line from the page 5 takeaways.

findings.summary: Page 6 resumes the networking topic — example diagram, rule-of-thumb callout and driver comparison — after page 5 already closed it with mistakes and a takeaways checklist.
findings.evidence: Page 5 ends with `5. Common Mistakes` and a `style:"checkbox"` summary; page 6 then starts with the flowchart "User-defined Network appnet", the callout "Rule of thumb", and `4. Comparison: Network Drivers`.
findings.fix: Move the appnet diagram and callout next to page 5's '3. Example: web talks to db', and place section 4 before section 5 so the networking chapter ends with its summary.

findings.summary: The registry topic is introduced by a paragraph and an image-trust table on the Compose page, two pages before the registry definition.
findings.evidence: Page 7 ends with "A ==registry== is where built images live so any host can `docker pull` them..." and a table of `Official` / `Verified publisher` / `Community` tiers, while `1. What a Registry Is` is on page 9.
findings.fix: Move both the intro paragraph and the trust-tier table to page 8/9 so they sit immediately before the registry definition.
